quote: Vorrichtung um einen Strom an mehreren Stellen beliebig einschalten und unterbrechen zu können u. zwar unabhängig von allen anderen Stellen
english: A device for being able to switch a current on and interrupt it at will at several places, and indeed independently of all other places
topic: The page completes an induction step (from n to n-1) in the proof of the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality, sketches a circuit for switching a current on and off independently from two or more places, and poses sphere-packing and circle-packing questions together with a related polygon minimization problem.

triage.modern_statement: Design a switching circuit with n ≥ 2 switch locations so that changing any one switch always toggles a single load (a current or lamp) between on and off, no matter how the other switches are set. In Boolean terms the load's state should be the parity (XOR) of the n switch states. This is the multiway switching problem (German: Wechselschaltung for two places, Kreuzschaltung for three or more). It is an electrical-engineering design puzzle, not a mathematical research question.
triage.answered_by: This is the standard solution used in building wiring; the sources found do not name an inventor or date. Two-way (3-way/SPDT) switches go at the two ends, and any number of intermediate switches (4-way/crossover, wired to swap the two traveler wires) go between them. This gives control from any number of places. Hilbert may have been thinking of this practice or puzzling it out himself; the note does not say which.

evidence.claim: Multiway switching means connecting two or more electrical switches so one load can be controlled from more than one location.

For more than two locations, two of the connecting wires pass through an intermediate switch that swaps the pair. Any number of intermediate switches can be added, so any number of locations is possible.

With one or more 4-way (intermediate) switches between 3-way switches at each end, the load can be controlled from three or more places, and flipping any switch turns the load on if it was off, or off if it was on.
In German usage, a Wechselschaltung switches from two places and a Kreuzschaltung from three or more.
A Kreuzschaltung lets you switch the same lighting independently from three or more places; for three places it uses two Wechselschalter with a Kreuzschalter between them.

triage.why: Hilbert asks for a way to switch a current on and off at several places, each independently of the others. That is exactly the standard multiway (Wechsel/Kreuz) switching problem, which is fully solved and routinely installed using end switches plus intermediate crossover switches. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem, and it is not a mathematical research question. The sources I found do not say when or by whom the circuit was first devised, so I cannot attribute it to anyone, and I cannot tell whether Hilbert worked it out himself or was recording known practice.
